agent_notes: The superscription is counted as word positions 1-3 of verse 1 (the KJV numbers it verse 0), so the glosses cover 20 words. 'Of Solomon' (lishlomoh) is rendered 'of Solomon' in both layers; the commentators split between 'by Solomon', 'about Solomon' and 'for Solomon' (Ibn Ezra and Radak read the lamed as 'on account of'), and the commentary says so.

STEPBible glosses H1004B bayit as 'a house' and 'ir as 'a city'; I kept the English indefinite in the literal layer but the commentary notes that the Hebrew has no article either, unlike the KJV's 'the house' and 'the city'.

history.note: [consider] Add 'Meiri on Psalms 127:1' to the shaqad note's sources. (PS.127.1: Meiri "ושקד הוא מלשון התמדה או לשון מהירות".)

agent_notes: The line 'ken yiten lididO shena' is genuinely ambiguous: 'so he gives sleep to his beloved' (sleep as the gift), 'he gives to his beloved while asleep' (so Radak, who reads shena as shena with alef for he), or 'thus' as 'in this way / likewise'. I kept 'sleep' as the object in the literal layer and put the alternative in the commentary. The five English versions split here: the BBE takes 'in sleep', the rest 'sleep'.
shena' is spelled with final alef where the usual form is shena (with he); Radak and Metzudat Zion both note this. The Masoretic text has no Ketiv/Qere here.

history.note: [consider] Consider 'So' or 'Thus' instead of 'Yet' in the dramatic layer, and 'kingship' alone for Radak. (PS.127.2: "כֵּן יִתֵּן לִידִידוֹ שֵׁנָא"; Radak: "כן נתן האל יתברך המלוכה בלא עמל לשלמה".)

agent_notes: Revised after the reviewer's requests. Commentary now says beten covers both belly and womb, that the KJV's 'womb' is accurate, and that the literal layer keeps 'belly' for its bodily register; the Genesis 25:23 example is removed. 'Not earned' is removed: sakhar is read by Ibn Ezra, Metzudat David and Malbim as a payment for deeds, given by YHWH; only the psalm's point that toil alone does not secure sons remains.

STEPBible glosses נחלת בנים as 'inheritance ... [is] sons'; I kept the verbless clause and bracketed 'is'. Rashi reads 'sons' as a teacher's disciples and the 'fruit of the belly' as the Torah in the heart; I mention it in a note but keep the plain sense in the translation. Rashi's quotation of Prov 22:18 is taken from the packet.
The Targum's 'good sons' and 'children of the womb' (ולדי מעא) are from the packet; I read the Targum's 'reward of good deeds' as supporting the deeds-reward reading, which is my inference.

agent_notes: The subject of 'they will not be ashamed' is unclear: the sons (ASV), the father (Radak mentions both) or both (Ibn Ezra). The dramatic layer keeps the plural 'they' and leaves the question open, as the Hebrew does.

STEPBible glosses 'et at position 12 as 'with'; I kept the gloss 'with' (dibber 'et is 'speak with') and noted in the commentary that some read it as 'speak against', which would make the gate a place of dispute rather than a courtroom of equals. I did not cite Meiri's long Talmudic reading (Kiddushin 30b), only the short Rashi reference, since I have not seen the passage itself.
